text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure, reduce stroke risk, and protect the kidneys in type 2 diabetes. Side effects range from mild, temporary reactions to rare, serious medical concerns, as detailed by the Mayo Clinic and GoodRx Health.
snippet_highlighted_words: mild, temporary reactions to rare, serious medical concerns

text_blocks.snippet: These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections (cold-like symptoms, stuffy or runny nose, sinus pressure)
Back or joint pain (arthralgia) and muscle cramps
Digestive issues (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or indigestion)

text_blocks.snippet: Contact a doctor or seek medical care right away if you experience:

list.snippet: Severe allergic reaction (angioedema): Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, hives, or trouble breathing and swallowing.
Severely low blood pressure (hypotension): Fainting, severe or ongoing dizziness, confusion, or blurred vision.
High potassium levels: Muscle weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat, or numbness and tingling.
Kidney problems: Sudden decrease in urination, swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet, or unexplained weight gain.
Liver problems: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or upper right stomach pain.
Pregnancy warning: Losartan can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby and must be stopped immediately if pregnancy is detected.

text_blocks.snippet: If you'd like, let me know:

list.snippet: What symptoms or side effects you are currently experiencing
Whether you just started taking losartan or had a dose change
Any other medications or supplements you take

text_blocks.snippet: I can help you understand what might be happening or what to discuss with your doctor.
